A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 25-page versions of the same Video Alchemist paper. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–D can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, a user preference study, and ablations in Tables 1–3, plus generated examples in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results, user study, ablations, and qualitative generation results, including the appendix examples.

M1.justification: The personalization architecture, image–word binding, augmentations, training procedure, and guidance-based inference remain unchanged. Self-conditioning is newly mentioned in the main text, but v1 already specifies its use in Table 5.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Panda-70M/internal training data and MSRVTT-Personalization benchmark. Subject, face, multi-subject, background-conditioning, and varied-reference scenarios are retained, including the same Appendix C examples.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain ELITE, VideoBooth, and DreamVideo for subject mode, and IP-Adapter, PhotoMaker, and Magic-Me for face mode. Appendix comparisons also remain unchanged; newly cited VideoDreamer and DisenStudio are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Metrics, the 1,736/1,285 subject/face test subsets, reference-image settings, 512×288 benchmark comparisons, and 256×144 ablations are unchanged. Both user studies use 200 samples per mode and five participants. No revised experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same image-encoder, word-token binding, and augmentation ablations in Table 3 and Figure 6, along with the same Appendix C conditioning analyses. The added attribution to Wu et al. does not introduce another experiment.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates and user preference percentages. Neither adds repeated-run or seed counts, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–3 are retained. For example, single-reference Video Alchemist still reports subject similarity 0.617 and face similarity 0.382. The qualitative examples and reported findings, including those in Appendix C, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The personalization-embedding formulation and both guidance equations in Appendix B.3 are unchanged. Visual inspection confirms that extraction differences in Equations (1)–(2) reflect encoding rather than mathematical revisions. No proofs or formal assumptions are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about multi-subject open-set personalization without test-time optimization, dataset construction and augmentation, and the personalization benchmark. Contributions and performance claims are not substantively broadened or narrowed.

C2.justification: Interpretations of encoder differences, image–word binding, copy-and-paste behavior, and reference-image tradeoffs remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same limitations concerning overfitting, segmented inputs, unnatural multi-subject composition, and the benchmark's lack of visual-quality assessment.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the benchmark from a promised release to a stated public release and supplies a repository address. Conversely, Table 5 removes the self-conditioning probability of 0.9 while retaining the indication that self-conditioning is used; no replacement probability is provided.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to VideoDreamer, DisenStudio, Analog Bits, Motion-conditioned Diffusion Model, and Neural Assets. Section 4.3 newly credits Wu et al. as inspiration for the encoder comparison. These additions refine attribution and related-work coverage without substantially changing the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes limited wording and punctuation edits, clarifies the RoPE description, and mentions existing self-conditioning in the main text. It adds a funding acknowledgment and disclaimer and cleans up bibliographic formatting and duplicate entries. Section order and narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The same 18 figures and six tables are retained, with unchanged figure imagery. Table 5 loses one hyperparameter row, while acknowledgment and reference additions cause localized reflow. There is no substantial redesign or reorganization.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves benchmark access documentation and attribution by reporting public availability, providing a repository address, and acknowledging additional related work and the encoder comparison's inspiration. Removing the self-conditioning probability slightly weakens reproducibility documentation. Overall, the access and attribution gains are limited but useful; the scientific methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
